Operand of the LDA at $1C04 (a list at $1B9B), low byte.
Operand of the LDA at $1C04, high byte.

Operand of the LDA at $1D74 (part image source), low byte.
Operand high byte.

Advances ($9A) to the next 64-byte sprite.

Operand of the LDA at $1E01, low byte.
Operand of the LDA at $1E01, high byte.
Advances the patched destination operands at $1F74-$1FCA by one sprite.
Decodes part image A mirrored: each row's three bytes are written in reverse order, bit-reversed through $BF00, zero runs as in $1D3D.
Self-modified operand of the mirrored decoder at $1F66: LDY source, low.
Self-modified operand of the mirrored decoder at $1F67: LDY source, high.
Self-modified operand of the mirrored decoder at $1F74: STA destination (row byte 2), low.
Self-modified operand of the mirrored decoder at $1F75: STA destination, high.
Self-modified operand of the mirrored decoder at $1F7B: LDY source, low (second byte).
Self-modified operand of the mirrored decoder at $1F7C: LDY source, high (second byte).
Self-modified operand of the mirrored decoder at $1F89: STA destination (row byte 1), low.
Self-modified operand of the mirrored decoder at $1F8A: STA destination (row byte 1), high.
Self-modified operand of the mirrored decoder at $1F90: LDY source, low (third byte).
Self-modified operand of the mirrored decoder at $1F91: LDY source, high (third byte).
Self-modified operand of the mirrored decoder at $1F9E: STA destination (row byte 0), low.
Self-modified operand of the mirrored decoder at $1F9F: STA destination (row byte 0), high.
Self-modified operand of the mirrored decoder at $1FB0: LDY run count, low.
Self-modified operand of the mirrored decoder at $1FB1: LDY run count, high.
Self-modified operand of the mirrored decoder at $1FBB: zero-run STA, low.
Self-modified operand of the mirrored decoder at $1FBC: zero-run STA, high.

Self-modified operand of the mirrored decoder at $1FC3: zero-run STA (second), high.

Build fighter X's sprite shape for this frame. Toggles the fighter's shape buffer ($4A,X bit 0), sets its sprite pointer $16,X = $25 + buffer (shapes at $C940/$C980/$C9C0/$CA00 via $1BC8/$1BD0), then copies 63 bytes from the animation frame source ($C000 when $4C,X is negative, else $1BD4/$1BC7 + $50/$52,X). If the frame's mirror flag ($54,X bit 4 >> 4) differs from facing $1E,X, the copy mirrors each row through the byte-reverse table $BF00 and swaps its outer bytes. Reached by JMP from $1CB0/$1CCE.

Turn the sprite shape at ($5A) upside down: swaps each of 30 bytes with its partner row given by the table at $20E1 (row r with row 20-r). Called after the copy when the frame's flag $56,X (attribute bit 5) is set.

Read the attributes of fighter X's animation frame $0477,X: $B533 low nibble - 1 -> $4C,X (shape source bank, negative = blank), $B4A1 -> $18,X and $B4EA -> $1A,X (per-frame offsets, not checked which axis), $B533 bit 7 -> $1C,X, bit 4 -> $54,X (mirror), bit 5 -> $56,X (vertical flip). Called from $1B24.
30 bytes: for each byte offset 0-29 of a sprite shape, the offset of the byte in the mirrored row (row r <-> row 20-r, three bytes a row). Read by flip_sprite_shape_vertically ($209F).
2 bytes, both $00 in both snapshots. Read by $1AA9, $1B06 and $1B6A (below $2000); purpose not traced.
Game entry, from $0402 and from the F5 key ($2465): reset the stack, JSR $1541, then run play_one_game for ever, each game starting from the first room.

One whole game. Clears the status rows, resets the score ($2468), zeroes sprite expansion and many state variables, sets the start room $046B from $0400 and map position $0469 from $0401, lives $2D32 = 1, copies the random seed $0430 to $042F, draws the energy bar row, resets the hero ($26C8). Loop at $2177: set up the room ($235C), draw the scroll icons ($2DAC); room $7A goes to the still ending scene ($2DB5). Then play ($21E2) until $0451 is set: $40 means a life was lost with lives left (back to $2177), otherwise game over: save a high score ($247F) and return.

The in-play main loop, one pass a frame. Waits while $0416 (pause, toggled by RESTORE through the NMI at $3C23) or $0411 (the frame handshake with the IRQ at $3F67) is set. Then: hero update ($055B); scroll pickup ($2C25), hazards ($2315) or the encounter scan ($27F5); the opponent when a fight is on; the two fighters ($32F9, $8F = the other one); the seed step ($2438) and the F5 key ($2444). Then sets $0411, redraws the energy bars ($2556), blinks icons ($2D57), steps the sound ($3E1A), and handles location types $05 ($2CE4) and $06 ($2CBC). Returns with A = 0 when $0451 (life lost) is set.

2 bytes ($69, $5A), indexed by the scroll direction $1535: the map position $72 at which, in a location of type $13 with $0461 = 0, $0462 is set to $80 and $08E0 is called (read at $22DB). What this event is in the game is not traced.

Per-frame update of the two hazard objects when $0464 is set: kind 1 moves objects 0 and 2 ($29FF) and ends the event when both are gone ($0D6E/$0D70); other kinds run $2B47 and, with $0464 bit 7, $2B9B.

Set up a room: waits for $0426; room $7A forces map position $4E; rooms $44-$4B (the meditation chambers) put the hero in move $26 with $1E = 1 at X $11. Converts start X $0481 x 8 into $0467/$0468 (adding $2436[$1E] when entering from a side, $0471), copies them to the hero position $DB/$DD and the map position $0469 to $72, loads the room ($0FEC, $168D, $1556), clears the object table, then waits for raster line $64 and draws ($11DA, $18BC).
2 bytes ($18, $00) by facing $1E: added to the hero's start X when entering a room from a side (read at $23B9).
Advance the random seed $0430 once a frame: shift left, EOR #$1D on carry (an 8-bit LFSR). The fighters' generator $3141 is seeded from it at the start of each game ($2162).

Scan keyboard row 0 ($DC00 = $FE, read $DC01). When the row changes to $BF (F5 alone, per the c64-reference matrix), JMP to game_restart; otherwise returns A = 0. The last value is kept in $0417 so F5 acts on the press only.
Set the six score digits $CC01-$CC06 (status screen, row 0) to five blanks and a 0: a digit byte 0 is blank, n shows digit n-1.
At game over: when the score $CC01-$CC06 is higher than the high score $CC21-$CC26 ($2488), copy it across ($249D).
Compare score digits $CC01.. with high-score digits $CC21.. from the left; carry clear means the score is higher.
Copy the six score digits $CC01-$CC06 to the high score $CC21-$CC26.
Add the score for the hero's landed move $045A: $051D[move] times 100 points (calls $24C3 that many times). Called from $3892 only when the hero (X = 0) and not the computer landed the hit.
Add 100 to the score: increments the hundreds digit $CC04 and carries into $CC03, $CC02, $CC01 (digit byte n shows n-1, 0 blank, $0B wraps to 1). Past 999,900 all digits become 0.

Subtract A from the energy of the fighter in $8F (entry $2545: fighter Y). The amount is written into the SBC operand at $254D; energy is floored at 0. $0412 is the hero's energy, $0413 the opponent's.
Second entry of damage_other_fighter: subtract A from the energy $0412,Y of fighter Y (floored at 0). Called from $2A5B and $2BB6 with Y = 0, the hero.
Operand of SBC #, written at run time by damage_other_fighter ($2545): the damage amount.
Draw both energy bars on the bottom status row ($CFC1-$CFE7): hero's energy $0412 from the left ($2563), opponent's $0413 from the right ($25D2).
Hero's bar: length energy/4, moved one step a frame towards it ($042C), drawn from column 1 of row 24 of the status screen with characters $1A-$1E and end cap $21.
Opponent's bar: length energy/4, one step a frame ($042D), drawn leftwards from column 36 of row 24 with characters $1A, $1B, $1F-$21.
Clear status row 24 ($CFC1-$CFE7), colour it $0F (light grey) in colour RAM $DBC1, and put the hero bar's end cap $21 in column 1.
Signed half-distances between fighter X and fighter Y from the X positions $DF/$E1: $0446 = (Y - X)/2, $0445 = (X - Y)/2.
Reset fighter X: clear its move state ($83, $7F, $96, $0414, $0452, $0456), set move $0C (standing) in $7D and $8B, pick its graphics set ($269D) and its fighting style ($314D).
From the graphics set $4E,X (0-4) load $5E,X, $48,X, $50,X and $52,X from the tables at $26C3, $26B4, $26B9, $26BE.
5 bytes by graphics set: value for $48,X (read at $26A4).
5 bytes by graphics set: low byte of the shape source, $50,X (read at $26A9).
5 bytes by graphics set: high part of the shape source, $52,X (read at $26AE).
5 bytes by graphics set: value for $5E,X (read at $269F).
Reset the hero at a game start: $1E = 0, energy $0412 and maximum $0485 = $2F (47), bar length 0, then reset_fighter.

Start an opponent from encounter entry $044E of the table at $E609: position from $E60B (or map position $72 + $2782[direction]) x 8 into $DC/$DE, $4F = flag bits 4-5 + 1; a low nibble of $0A or more marks a group ($0491/$0492, random $4F, $0423 = random 1-8). Energy $0413 = random 31-63, +64 once 16 opponents have been beaten ($048C). Fighter 1 is reset and walks in (move $0D).
2 bytes ($FB, $2D) by scroll direction $1535: offset from the map position at which an opponent enters (read at $2708).
At game start: clear bit 7 (done) of every 3-byte entry of the encounter table $E609 (count in $E608) and the eight scroll flags $0405-$040C.

After an opponent dies: for an entry whose low nibble is $0A another opponent comes ($26E9) until $0472 runs out or scroll flag $0409 is negative (delivered); otherwise the fight ends: $0462 = $80, then end_fight.
No fight: $044B = 1, opponent energy 0, $044E = $80 (no entry), $0475/$0A7E cleared, movement-only move set ($0C19).

Look for an entry of the encounter table $E609 (3 bytes: flags, room, position) in this room ($046B) at this map position $72. Done entries (flags bit 7) come back only after 30 defeats ($048C), at random. Flags bit 6 clear: a fight starts (spawn_opponent; if the hero's move has $0493 bit 7 he is put in move $29 and sample 3 plays); bit 6 set: a hazard ($28B6); bits 6 and 5: a scroll lying in the room ($291F).
2 bytes ($00, $29) by scroll direction $1535: added to the map position when placing a scroll or matching an entry (read at $2857, $294E).
Start object X (0 or 2) of the object table at the position $0433/$0434 + $2994/$2996[direction $0D7C], Y $C6, step $FC, active ($0D6E = 2).
2 bytes: high byte of the start offset for a hazard object, by direction (read at $2973, $2ABD, $2B1E).
2 bytes: low byte of the start offset for a hazard object, by direction (read at $296A, $2AB4, $2B15).
Hazard kind 2: unless a fight is on, place object X at a random distance $48-$87 right of the hero, or $40-$7F left of him ($0D7C = side), Y $C6, step $12.

Per-frame for hazard object X. On sprite contact with the hero (collision bits $047F & $053B): if the hero is at the striking frame of an attack ($04E1 per move) and the object is inside hazard_hit_margin, it is knocked away (sample 1, step $0D); otherwise the hero loses 2 energy. Then it moves ($0C53) and, once off screen, restarts up to $0463 times.
12 bytes by hero move $00-$0B: margin added to or taken from the hero's X when testing a hazard object's hit (read at $2A3C, $2A6C).
Hazard kinds other than 1: move object 0 ($0C53); when it reaches step $26, start object 2 from it (Y $0F, $0D7A = $37) and set $0464 = $82.
2 bytes ($00, $0C) by $0D7C: X offset of the second object from the first (read at $2B85).
The second object of a kind-$82 hazard: on sprite contact the hero loses 10 energy and sample 2 plays; otherwise it moves and is removed past the hero's position.

While a scroll lies in the room ($0464 = $FF): on sprite contact with the hero, mark its entry done, set scroll flag $0405 + (flags & 7) to 1 and draw its icon; remove it when it scrolls off the screen.

$0447 = 1 when the fighters' columns $E5/$E6 are 18 or more apart. Then $0489 = 1 when the opponent's column is 0-9 or 28-34 past the map position $72, 0 when it is 10-27 or apart is 0; room $3F always 0.

In a meditation chamber (location type 6): the chamber is room $44 + n; if scroll n has been found ($0405+n = 1) mark it delivered ($80), add a life ($2D32), colour its icon red. The room becomes the respawn point $2D33. Then blink ($2D70).

Location type 5: blink icon 7, and unless scroll 8 is delivered ($040C negative) flash multicolour $C1 and drain 1 hero energy every 10 frames; at 0 the hero dies (move $1A). Elsewhere: +1 energy every 128 frames up to $0485, except while $0462 = 1.
Frame counter for energy_regen: 128 frames (10 in a type-5 location).
Lives: 1 at the start of a game ($2154), +1 for each scroll delivered ($2CCD), -1 on death ($353E); zero ends the game.
The room the hero restarts in after losing a life: the last meditation chamber visited ($2CBF, read at $3548).
Colour row 1 of the status area ($D828-$D84F) yellow (7). Also called from $C4CE.
Clear row 1 of the status screen ($CC28-$CC4F), where the scroll icons go. Also called from $C4D1.
X = Y x 3: the screen offset of scroll icon Y ($CC30 + X).
While $0491 is set, blink icon $0492 every 20 frames ($0490), counting $0491 down; then redraw it.
Every 20 frames toggle $048F and draw or blank scroll icon Y.
Seven bytes no code reaches: LDA $046B / SEC / SBC #$44 / TAY (room number to chamber number).
Draw scroll icon Y (two characters from $054B/$0553) at $CC30 + 3Y if flag $0405+Y is set, otherwise blank it.
Write the two characters of scroll icon Y ($054B,Y and $0553,Y) at $CC30,X / $CC31,X.
Draw the eight scroll icons.

Room $7A: expand sprites 1 and 5 ($22) in both directions behind the background, place two objects, then loop for ever flashing object 0 ($0D6A) and polling F5 ($2444), the only way out. Seen as the game's end only by this reading; not checked live.

Computer fighter X picks its next move into $8D,X (and $AD,X). Uses the other fighter's move ($8B,Y via $8F), their distance ($0445/$0446), the style set up by $314D, reaction timers ($045B, $045F, $AB, $AF) and the random generator $3141. Runs a scripted combination through the table at $3288 when $B4,X is set ($3233).
Three bytes no code reaches: JMP $2F6C.

Second half of opponent_ai. $30A3: a chosen move $07 is kept for fighter types $0422 below 7 and becomes $0D for 7 and up. $30AE: move $03 is taken only by types 2 and up. $30BD: start combination 5 with move $0F. $30C8: attacks chosen by distance when both face the same way (tables $32DB, $32F1). $311E: moves $08/$09 are rolled against $0470: negative gives $13, $40 and up $0E, $20-$3F $11, else the move stands.
Random number: shift $042F left, EOR #$1D on carry (an 8-bit LFSR). Returns it in A.
Set the computer fighter's style from its type $0422,X: aggression mask $32B0 -> $0470, move mask $32BC -> $B3, reaction time random 7-31 -> $AA/$046E, timers reset, $045D random $3F-$7F.
AI combination 1 (table $3288): move $0F until a random roll (random AND $85 = 0) or the other fighter's frame is $15, then move $03 and end.
AI combination 3: move $07, end the combination.
AI combination 4: move $12, end the combination.
AI combination 5: move $0F until $96,X is set, then move $02 and end.
AI combination 8: at random, combination 6, or combination 5 after setting $B4 (not $B4,X) to 5.
AI combination 6: move $01 or $0B at random, end the combination.
AI combination 7: move $03 when $1E,X equals the other fighter's $1E, else $09; end.
AI combination 2: move $03 until the fighter is in move $03, then end.
Dispatch AI combination $B4,X (1-9) through the address table at $3288: JMP ($B6).
A = a chosen AI move. If the other fighter is in move $02, $03, $09 or $0F, half the time replace it with a random one from $32F1.
AI combination 9: for fighter types 7 and up, half the time move $06 and end; otherwise switch to combination 1.
10 addresses by $B4 x 2: 0 unused ($0000), then combinations 1-9 at $319A, $3221, $31BC, $31C7, $31D2, $31F7, $320B, $31E8, $326A.
High byte of entry 0 of ai_combo_table (read at $323A as the high byte of every entry).
12 bytes by the other fighter's move $00-$0B: combination to start in answer (0 none; 2 only when $0474,X is clear). Read at $2F0F.
4 bytes: random answer when the other fighter is in move $14 (read at $302D).
4 bytes: random answer when the other fighter is in move $15 (read at $301B).
12 bytes by fighter type $0422: mask for the random attack roll, stored in $0470 (read at $315F).
12 bytes by fighter type: mask stored in $B3, ANDed with a random number to choose idle, answer or attack (read at $317D).
19 bytes: attack moves chosen by distance when facing away, index distance + random 0-3 (read at $3077).
22 bytes: attack moves chosen by distance when facing the same way, index distance + $21 + random 0-3 (read at $30E1).
8 bytes: moves $0C-$13 picked at random for walking and dodging (read at $3044, $310B, $3266, $3371).

Per-frame update of fighter X (other fighter in $8F): resolve death and falls ($3504), test its strike ($376D), choose the next move (AI or joystick, $3343), location actions ($3664), commit it ($33F6), animate ($373F). Then reads the sprite-to-sprite collision register $D01E (bits 0-2): with no contact and an attack move $01-$0B, $20 = X.

Next move for fighter X into $8D,X: a dying fighter keeps $0452,X; location type $1D forces move $1B with $1E = 0; the computer ($0454,X set) uses opponent_ai, where a move $17 or above becomes a random one from $32F1 and a move not allowed now (table $33E3) becomes $0C or $0E; the hero reads the joystick.

Read fighter X's joystick: $DC00 for X = 0 (port 2), $DC01 for X = 1 (port 1). Fire goes to $0418,X. When $1E,X is non-zero left and right are swapped, then the 5 bits index the move table $33C3; a move the table $33E3 does not allow becomes $0C (stand).

32 bytes: move code by the joystick bits (fire, right, left, down, up; 0 = pressed), as seen by a fighter with $1E = 0. No fire: up $10, down $0F, right $0D, left $0E, up-right $01, down-right $02, up-left $12, down-left $11. Fire: up $07, down $03, right $05, left $0A, up-right $06, down-right $04, up-left $08, down-left $09. Nothing, or fire alone: $0C.

19 bytes, one per move $00-$12, rewritten at run time: 1 = the move may be used now. $0C19 (below $2000) allows only $0A and $0C-$12 out of a fight, $0C33 allows all in one, and $0C3E then forbids $03, $07, $09, $10, $11, $12 while $0474 is set.
move_allowed entry for move $03: cleared by $0C40 while $0474 is set.
move_allowed entry for move $07: cleared by $0C43 while $0474 is set.
move_allowed entry for move $09: cleared by $0C46 while $0474 is set.
move_allowed entry for move $0A: set by $0C20 even out of a fight.
move_allowed entry for move $10: cleared by $0C49 while $0474 is set.
move_allowed entry for move $11: cleared by $0C4C while $0474 is set.
move_allowed entry for move $12: cleared by $0C4F while $0474 is set.

Make the chosen move $8D,X the current move $8B,X, with the rules for moves in progress: $17/$1A (death) commit at once (sample 4 for types $38/$3C); some moves turn into $0F, $13, $16 or $0C depending on the move being left and $0493.

When $047D,X is set: a dying fighter ($0452,X) ends. Opponent dead: mark its encounter done, count the defeat ($048C, max 31), go to opponent_beaten. Hero dead: $0451 = 1, a life is lost; with lives left $0451 = $40 and the hero restarts in respawn_room. Otherwise ends falls and the location actions of moves $18-$28 (climbing and the like, through $0796/$07CB/$0700/$0809; $26 meditation refills energy).

For the hero: joystick moves $0E, $0F, $10 become location actions by the location flags $0473 and the tile under him (($E7),Y): $18, $1C, $22, $24 or $13. In room $34 also sets blink $0491/$0492. Moves $0E also turn into the counter of the other fighter's attack ($04BD) when in range.
If fighter X's move changed, restart its animation (sample 3 for an attack, $01-$0B); then step the animation ($1A73).
When fighter X's attack reaches its striking frame ($04E1 per move = frame $0477,X), and it is not falling, test the hit ($379C).

Is the other fighter within the reach of fighter X's move? The reach comes from the tables pointed to by $04ED (facing each other) or $0505 (same way) indexed by the target's frame, and $04C9/$04D5. On a hit: damage $052F[move] ($2543) and score for the hero ($24A9). At 0 energy the target dies ($0452 = $17 or $1A); sample 2 for moves $02, $05, $0B and for some others, sample 1 otherwise.
A = 1 when the other fighter's attack could reach fighter X (distance $14-$EF when facing each other, $03-$1F otherwise, by $04C9), else 0.
An RTS called three times from test_hit ($38CA, $38E7, $3904): a hook that does nothing.
Meditation: the maximum energy $0485 = 47 + 4 x (defeats $048C rounded down to even), at most 127, and the hero's energy $0412 is filled to it.

Raster handler of the sprite multiplexer. A CIA1 interrupt goes to the sample player ($3D8B). Otherwise sets the Y of sprites 1-3 and their three pointers, the next raster line and the next handler, from operands the code at $41B5-$4530 and $480E-$4823 writes each frame; even the pointers' page is patched ($F3F9 on the play-area screen, $CFF9 on the status screen). In f2-play: Y $B1, pointers 4/5/0, next $39C0 at line $C5.
